findings.message: Pattern 7 still documents the old delete-entry shape, saying the deleted entry must carry the baseline `kind`/shape and the example includes `role`, `kind`, `methods`, and `docs`. The generate+annotate workflow and implementation now make `catalog import --action delete` write an identity-only tombstone with just `action`, optional `module_path`, `spec_refs`, and `informal_grounds`; `.harness/capabilities/type-designer.md` says the same. Leaving this stale cookbook rule in the relocated schema reference will make reviewers/designers treat correct generated delete tombstones as incomplete and may lead them to hand-add fields the CLI intentionally omits.

The reference-entry cookbook says an empty `methods: []` is acceptable when no rendering fidelity is required. That contradicts the binding kind-selection convention's R7/reference semantics, which requires baseline ports declared as `action: "reference"` to enumerate the baseline methods, and it also conflicts with the capability's 12c baseline-identical attestation for every reference entry. This weakens the policy exactly where type-designer will look after the relocation and can cause under-specified reference entries to pass author review despite violating the project convention.

`sotp catalog init` is documented as producing only “5 header keys”, but the implementation builds six top-level keys: `schema_version`, `crate_name`, `layer`, `types`, `traits`, and `functions`. The same incorrect count is repeated in `knowledge/conventions/catalogue-schema-reference.md`, so the capability/checklist can make a valid generated skeleton look non-conforming. Update the documented count to six while keeping the note that empty impl arrays are omitted.

T001 is ordered before T002 but includes adding references to `knowledge/conventions/catalogue-schema-reference.md` `(T002)`. T002 is the task that creates and registers that manual, so executing T001 first leaves an individually committed task with references to a missing artifact and can break reference verification. Move T002 before T001, or split the T001 reference update into a task that runs after T002.

P1 upstream restatement: `T002`, `T001`, `T003`, and sections `S1`-`S3` go beyond target + operation + anchor cite by restating upstream spec behavior in prose, e.g. the exact authority-note semantics, generated-output workflow, receipt criteria, boundary-section rule, and stale-pointer rationale. `knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md` and the impl-plan severity policy require these downstream plan texts to reference `IN-*`/`CN-*`/`AC-*` anchors instead of re-explaining the behavior contract, otherwise the plan can drift from `spec.json`. Trim the descriptions to file/symbol targets, concrete operations, and the existing anchor cites.

CN-01 says the `.harness/capabilities/type-designer.md` rewrite is limited to IN-01..IN-03 plus IN-07's 12a receipt text, but IN-04/IN-05 and AC-03/AC-06 require removing schema/cookbook sections from that same doc and adding a reference to the new manual. Downstream implementers cannot satisfy both the constraint and the in-scope/AC requirements deterministically.

GO-02 makes the separate reference document a goal, but its only adr_ref is D2. D2 moves schema knowledge out of the type-designer workflow; the decision to keep that knowledge in an independent `knowledge/conventions/` manual is D9, so this goal is not anchored to the decision that authorizes the reference-document outcome.
findings.category: goal not anchored to a decision
